goal: Understand reentrancy attack mechanics, call ordering, and practical defenses.
knowledgePoints: External calls transfer control to potentially adversarial code.
Reentrancy exposes an intermediate state before the first invocation finishes.
A withdrawal that sends before clearing a balance can reuse stale accounting.
An attacker receive function recursively calls the vulnerable entry point.
The exploit requires a bounded stopping condition to avoid reverting from gas exhaustion.
Checks-Effects-Interactions commits all related state before external interaction.
ReentrancyGuard is defense in depth and must cover the invariant boundary.
Cross-function and cross-contract paths can share the same broken invariant.
Read-only reentrancy exposes temporarily invalid values to another protocol.
Pull payments isolate delivery but still require protected withdrawal logic.
Using call requires checking success and assuming the recipient is adversarial.
Adversarial and invariant tests should verify both storage and asset conservation.
